name: VINU public addLiquidityETH() moves 80% of any address's balance and calls a caller-supplied router
summary: VINU's addLiquidityETH(routeraddr, lpraddr, devaddr) has no access control: it moves 80% of devaddr's VINU balance into the token contract and then calls a router named by the caller. The attacker bought a little VINU, called it four times with a fake router and devaddr set to the VINU/WETH pair, stripping about 99.8% of the pair's VINU, synced the pair and swapped its VINU for the pair's WETH.
notes: The exploit came 96 blocks after deployment; the deployer had launched the pair with 2 ETH through the same function and the real router, then renounced ownership. The anchor is the pair's only WETH outflow above 0.3 ETH since creation. Loss is the pair's WETH net of the attacker's 0.1 ETH buy; its VINU is unpriced and valued at nothing (rule 12).
